content.text:
`ShapeIndex` now has `Encode(io.Writer)` and `Decode(io.Reader)`. It's committed as `8b2ee73` on a new branch, `shapeindex-encoding`. There's no `main` branch in this repo, so I branched from `master`. The full test suite passes with the race detector on.

**What's in it** (`s2/shapeindex_encode.go`):
- **Shapes and IDs:** every shape is written with its ID, and removed IDs stay as gaps. New shapes added after decoding get the next ID, so existing cell references stay valid.
- **Shape types:** `Polygon`, `Loop`, `Polyline`, `PointVector`, `LaxPolyline`, `LaxPolygon` and `LaxLoop` all decode back to the same type. For `Polygon` and `Loop`, loop order, depth, origin-inside flag and bounds are stored, so edge numbering is exactly the same. Any other shape (in practice the test-only `edgeVectorShape`) decodes as a generic edge list that keeps its edges, chains, dimension and reference point.
- **Cell structure:** all cells and their contents are stored. A decoded index is ready to query and iterate without `Build`. `Encode` applies pending updates itself, so an index that was never built still encodes completely.
- **Edge cases:** an empty index encodes to a few bytes, not zero. Shapes with no edges (empty or full polygons and loops, empty polylines and point vectors) and shapes with several chains all round-trip.
- **Bad input:** truncated data, unknown shape kinds, invalid or out-of-order cell IDs, links to unknown shapes and out-of-range edge IDs all return errors. Counts have upper limits and buffers grow only as data actually arrives, so a fake huge count can't trigger a huge allocation. On error the target index is left unchanged.

**Tests** (`s2/shapeindex_encode_test.go`) cover round-trips of every shape type, comparing cells, query results and the bytes after re-encoding. They also check empty and zero-edge shapes, mixed chains, preserved IDs, encoding without `Build`, truncation at every byte, flipped bytes at every position (no panics), and hand-made oversized counts.

**Problems in the existing code:**
- **Fixed:** shapes removed before `Build` caused later shapes to be silently left out of the index, because the build loop counted shapes instead of using the next ID. I changed it to loop up to `nextID`, and it's included in the same commit.
- **Not fixed:** adding shapes to an index that has already been built (or decoded) and has shapes, then building again, deadlocks. `shrinkToFit` calls `s.Iterator()`, which tries to take the lock its caller already holds. The same happens with a normal index, not just a decoded one.
- **Not fixed:** removing a shape after `Build` was never implemented, so cells still point to the removed shape. The encoder skips those stale entries.

I kept the new tests away from the two unfixed paths. Fixing them is separate work; I can take it on if you want.
